answer: Threshold shareholding resists sybils. Each key locks a slashable deposit and holds exactly one share in a periodically reshared group. A public prism of dealers issues fresh shares bound to a single pubkey. A missed ceremony or a share already recorded for another identity slashes every linked deposit. Attendance and share commitments sit on a public knoll until the next reshare. Ceremonies follow a published falcon schedule, so one process cannot carry many shares. Fielding N identities needs N distinct live share-holders and N deposits, so availability and capital scale with farm size.
